messages.subject: Re: CONSULTATION--estimating precision at the 'sub-population'
parts:
Chunlin:

Thank you for the additional information about your study. The survey=20
design you employed (having between one and 3 transects per stratum). =20
This will give you a poor estimate of encounter rate variability within=20
each stratum. In fact for strata in which you placed only a single=20
transect, Distance will report that encounter rate variance is presumed=20
to be zero (because it cannot be estimated). By ignoring that source of=20
variability, you may find (perversely) that your smallest confidence=20
intervals are produced in those strata where you placed but a single=20
transect.

Lesson to learn: if you wish to estimate density at the level of the=20
stratum, place enough replicate transects (15-20) within the strata to=20
produce a believable estimate of encounter rate variance within the strat=
a.

> > Thank you very much for your immediate reply to me. I surveyed nine=20
> > sites where one to three transect lines were laid repectively=20
> > according to the specific topography aiming to have a good visibility=20
> > throughout the whole area surveyed and to reduce the influence of=20
> > topopraphy. In each site, more than 60 clusters were detected. Data=20
> > (excluding the number of calves to avoid the possible=20
> > autocorrelation) from these nine field surveys were analyzed=20
> > seperately. Three widest 95% confidence intervals (CV) of estimated=20
> > density in some sub-population were 1.165-54.841 (50.8%), =20
> > 0.883-62.618 (37.2%) and 1.265-175.299 (67.7%).
> > Another point for clarifying my problem is that the distribution area=20
> > of each sub-population is relatively small (about 1000ha). In some=20
> > areas where the focal species was distributed relatively evenly, only=20
> > one transect lines was designed aiming to avoid repeated record of=20
> > individuals in the case of more than one line. And at most three lines=20
> > were established in any site.
